grade.rationale: The implementation is readable and uses create-only files and durable flushes thoughtfully, but archive correctness is undermined by globally duplicate run IDs, unsafe dot-segment IDs, failure under concurrent appends, and brittle recovery from interrupted writes. The available .NET build analyzer reported no findings; test coverage is unknown.

summary: The archive model and serialization layout are clear, but the store does not fully enforce its identity and append-only guarantees. Duplicate run IDs can be created in different month directories, special run IDs can escape the intended per-run layout, concurrent writers receive sharing violations, and one interrupted append can make an entire JSONL stream unreadable. Schema versions are emitted but not validated when loading, and attempt ordering fails beyond four digits.

grade.rationale: Run identity is not globally unique, dot-segment IDs violate directory isolation, parallel appends can fail, and attempt ordering becomes incorrect at attempt 10000.
The records and persistence methods are well organized, but schema compatibility and archive invariants are implicit rather than centralized and enforced.
Names, comments, JSON ordering, and the separation between history and recovery data communicate intent well.
I/O exceptions remain visible, but interrupted JSONL writes poison subsequent reads and deserialization errors lack archive-record context.

The small synchronous API is straightforward to exercise with temporary directories, though direct static filesystem access makes concurrency, partial-write, and I/O-failure scenarios difficult to test deterministically. Coverage is unknown.

findings.title: A run ID can be created more than once in different months
findings.description: CreateRun derives the destination solely from CreatedAt and never checks whether the same RunId already exists elsewhere in the archive. Creating an existing ID with a different month therefore succeeds. Later lookups select the first matching month in ordinal order, so operations and attempts may be written to a different run than the newly created record.
findings.recommendation: Before creating a run, perform a global ID lookup and reject any existing match. For race-safe cross-process behavior, maintain an atomic ID index or otherwise reserve the run ID independently of its month partition.

findings.title: Dot-segment run IDs bypass the per-run directory boundary
findings.description: The basename and separator checks accept values such as "." and "..". Path.Combine then resolves those values to the month directory or archive root rather than a dedicated run directory, allowing files for such a run to pollute archive structural directories and causing misleading lookup results.
findings.recommendation: Reject "." and ".." explicitly, reject invalid or reserved filename forms for the supported platforms, and verify that the normalized candidate remains an immediate child of the intended month directory.

findings.title: Concurrent append operations fail with sharing violations
findings.description: AppendLine opens the JSONL file for read/write while granting only FileShare.Read. A second operation or finding append that overlaps the first cannot open the file for writing and will throw IOException. This is especially problematic for a review runner that may complete operations in parallel, because observations are not reliably appendable under normal concurrency.
findings.recommendation: Serialize appends per archive file and add an appropriate cross-process locking strategy if multiple processes are supported. Keep each record append inside the lock and define bounded retry behavior for transient sharing violations.

findings.title: An interrupted final append makes the complete JSONL stream unreadable
findings.description: WriteThrough and Flush improve durability but do not make a record append indivisible. A crash or disk failure can leave a truncated final line. LoadLines then attempts to deserialize that line and throws, preventing callers from retrieving all earlier valid observations.
findings.recommendation: Detect an unterminated or malformed trailing record and recover the valid prefix while reporting the damaged tail. Consider length framing or checksums if stronger corruption detection is required, and include the file path and record number in reported errors.

findings.title: Archive schema identifiers and versions are not validated when reading
findings.description: Deserialize accepts records with any $schema or SchemaVersion value. Consequently, a future or unrelated schema can be materialized as the current type and interpreted with current semantics, defeating the compatibility boundary implied by the versioned archive records.
findings.recommendation: After deserialization, validate the expected schema ID and supported version for each record type and throw a contextual compatibility exception for unknown versions. Add explicit migration handling if older versions must remain readable.

findings.title: Lexical filename sorting misorders attempts after 9999
findings.description: Attempt filenames use a minimum width of four digits, but LoadAttempts sorts them lexically. Attempt 10000 therefore sorts before portions of the four-digit sequence rather than after attempt 9999.
findings.recommendation: Sort loaded records by their numeric Attempt property, parse the numeric filename for ordering, or enforce a documented maximum that cannot exceed the filename width.
